title: Eighth Word Applying The Symbols Divine Unity Grave And Death

questions.question: What happens when a person makes this short worldly life his biggest goal?
questions.answer: He lives in a bad state inside, even if life looks nice on the outside.

questions.question: If someone truly turns toward the life that lasts forever, what does he receive?
questions.answer: He gets happiness in this life and in the next life.

questions.question: Which life in the passage is short and does not last?
questions.answer: Life in this world.

questions.question: Which life in the passage lasts forever?
questions.answer: The life to come.

questions.question: How might this world feel for a person who cares about the next life?
questions.answer: It may feel hard and upsetting.

questions.question: Why can that person keep going even when life is hard?
questions.answer: He sees this world as a place to wait before Paradise.

questions.question: What good actions does that person do while facing hardship?
questions.answer: He stays patient and thanks Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage teach us to chase only this world or to care most about the next life?
questions.answer: It teaches us to care most about the next life.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: We should not make this world our main goal; we should aim for the life to come.

questions.question: What kind of life is this world called in the passage?
questions.answer: A life that passes quickly.

questions.question: Can someone look happy on the outside but still be in a very bad condition inside?
questions.answer: Yes. A person may seem to be in a good place but still be miserable inside.

questions.question: Who receives the happiness of both worlds?
questions.answer: The person who sincerely aims for eternal life.

questions.question: What does “both worlds” mean here?
questions.answer: This life and the next life.

questions.question: What picture is used to describe this world for a believer?
questions.answer: A waiting place before Paradise.

questions.question: How should a person act while waiting through the hard parts of life?
questions.answer: With patience and thankfulness.

questions.question: If life is tough, does that mean a person has no happiness at all?
questions.answer: No. A person who aims for the next life can still have real happiness.

questions.question: In the passage, what mistake does a person make if he lives only for this world?
questions.answer: He makes the world his main purpose.

questions.question: What is wrong with making only this world your purpose?
questions.answer: It leads to inner misery, even if things seem pleasant.

questions.question: What kind of turning toward eternal life is mentioned?
questions.answer: A serious and sincere turning.

questions.question: What reward comes from that sincere turning?
questions.answer: Happiness in both lives.

questions.question: According to the passage, can this world still be painful for a good person?
questions.answer: Yes. It can still be difficult and sad.

questions.question: What thought helps that person bear the pain?
questions.answer: Thinking of this world as only a waiting room before Paradise.

questions.question: What two beautiful qualities are named at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Patience and thankfulness.

questions.question: Which person is doing better in the passage: the one who loves only this world, or the one who prepares for the next life?
questions.answer: The one who prepares for the next life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person whose heart is tied only to this world?
questions.answer: That person is in a terrible inner state.

questions.question: Even if a person seems to be surrounded by nice things, can he still be unhappy inside?
questions.answer: Yes. Outside comfort does not always mean true happiness.

questions.question: What should a person face toward with real care and effort?
questions.answer: The everlasting life.

questions.question: What kind of happiness comes from that choice?
questions.answer: Happiness here and in the hereafter.

questions.question: How is this world described for the person who believes and stays focused on the next life?
questions.answer: Like a place to wait before entering Paradise.

questions.question: When troubles come, what does that person do instead of giving up?
questions.answer: He endures and thanks Allah.

questions.question: What does this teach about hard times?
questions.answer: Hard times can be borne with patience when we remember what comes after.

questions.question: Is the passage more about outside looks or about a person’s real goal?
questions.answer: It is about a person’s real goal.

questions.question: What is one big contrast in the passage?
questions.answer: One person lives only for this world, and another lives for the eternal life.

questions.question: Which person ends up with true happiness?
questions.answer: The one who aims for the eternal life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the person who only wants worldly life?
questions.answer: He is in a painful condition, even if things look beautiful.

questions.question: What does “apparently in Paradise” mean in simple words?
questions.answer: Life may look wonderful on the outside.

questions.question: What does the person focused on the next life get besides future reward?
questions.answer: Happiness in this life too.

questions.question: Why does he not fall apart when life is difficult?
questions.answer: He knows this world is only a place before Paradise.

questions.question: What are the two ways he responds to suffering?
questions.answer: He is patient and thankful.

questions.question: What should a Muslim child learn from this passage?
questions.answer: To love the next life more than this world and to be patient and thankful to Allah.

questions.question: What should not be the biggest aim of our life, according to the passage?
questions.answer: This passing worldly life.

questions.question: Why is it not wise to make this world our highest goal?
questions.answer: Because it leads to real unhappiness inside.

questions.question: What should be our greater goal instead?
questions.answer: The life that never ends.

questions.question: What does a person gain when he truly seeks that lasting life?
questions.answer: Joy in both this world and the next.

questions.question: Does the passage promise that this world will always be easy for such a person?
questions.answer: No. It may still be hard and painful.

questions.question: What understanding helps him stay strong?
questions.answer: He sees this life as a short waiting place before Paradise.

questions.question: What attitude does he show while he waits?
questions.answer: He is patient and grateful.

questions.question: If two people both have hard lives, which one is better off in the passage?
questions.answer: The one who looks toward eternal life and thanks Allah with patience.
